findings.title: The dark-theme color uses the wrong lightness
findings.body: This rule originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new light-theme branch is 70%. The change should preserve the original 30% branch and use the complementary 70% adjustment on `$secondary`; as written, topic metadata links become substantially lighter in light themes and use the wrong shade in dark themes.

findings.title: The modal hint lightness was changed instead of preserved
findings.body: The existing hint color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new light-theme branch is 30%, with the complementary dark-theme branch also reversed. This changes the hint's appearance in light themes and selects the wrong shade in dark themes; retain 70% for `$primary` and use 30% for `$secondary`.

findings.title: Topic-map heading lightness was changed
findings.body: This heading previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the new expression uses 50% for both theme branches. That makes the heading a different shade even in light themes and loses the intended 80% complementary adjustment for dark themes.

findings.title: Group member names no longer use their original lightness
findings.body: The original rule used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but this replacement uses 50% for both branches. Consequently group member names change shade in light themes and do not receive the corresponding 70% `$secondary` adjustment in dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness was changed
findings.body: This heading previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the replacement uses 50% for both branches. This changes the heading shade in light themes and fails to use the complementary 80% adjustment for dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile group member names no longer use their original lightness
findings.body: The original rule used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the replacement uses 50% for both branches. Group member names therefore change shade in light themes and do not use the corresponding 70% `$secondary` adjustment in dark themes.
